Across APEC’s business landscape, with AI abundant but originality scarce, the organizations pulling ahead are redesigning the work, building on what only their people can do, and learning faster than their peers. Leading this change is the CEO’s job.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is profoundly reshaping the way work gets done across the APEC economies and India.

This report sponsored by Deloitte Asia Pacific explores the "Originality Gap" between adopting AI and creating distinctive business value. As intelligence becomes commoditized, advantage increasingly comes from what cannot be bought: unique experience, human judgement, customer trust, and an organization’s ability to learn and adapt.

Leaders expected to pull ahead are those who are not simply deploying AI but rethinking the business and its possible futures.

When everyone can access the same AI, advantage comes from what a company can uniquely create, learn or own.

The organizations expected to pull ahead use AI not just to improve efficiency, but to redesign how their business creates value.

As AI takes on more execution, advantage increasingly depends on how human judgement, creativity and insight is amplified by AI.

Original advantage compounds through deliberate learning.

Sustainable AI advantage comes from learning faster than competitors and turning every lesson into advantage that nobody can copy.

AI isn’t just a tech challenge. It’s about rethinking the business and its possible futures, defining what AI is for your organisation. The result is a company’s intelligence signature, and shaping it is the CEO’s work.

Simply having AI is no longer an advantage. It's the floor everyone stands on.

Robert Hillard, CEO, Deloitte Asia Pacific

As AI takes on more of the work, the value of people doesn't decline. It shifts

The Deloitte Asia Pacific CEO AI Leadership Report sponsored by Deloitte Asia Pacific is based on a survey of 1,278 business leaders across 18 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies and India. While India is not an APEC member, it was included in recognition of its important role in the emerging AI ecosystem and strong links with APEC member economies. Respondents represent more than a dozen major industries and include large global enterprises, national leaders, and organizations at the forefront of innovation in emerging sectors. The survey was complemented by follow-up interviews with 50 CEOs and senior business leaders from organizations demonstrating advanced levels of AI adoption and integration.
